name: Hohhot Baita International Airport
before:
Inner Mongolia's largest airport, 14.3 km east of downtown Hohhot, handling just over 12.7 million passengers in 2025. A metro station on Line 1 serves the terminal, which keeps the transfer into the city simple.

The network is broader than the passenger figure suggests. For 2025 the airport planned 139 routes serving 92 cities, of which 83 are nonstop and six are international or regional, so connections across northern China are good even though long haul is limited.

It also does a serious amount of freight. Cargo passed 60,000 tonnes for the first time in 2025, and the mix says a lot about the region: more than 6,000 tonnes of that was fresh meat, with cold chain veterinary pharmaceuticals up by almost a third on the year.

Baita means White Pagoda, after the Wanbu Huayanjing Pagoda a few kilometres south east of the airport, which is one of the sights of Hohhot.
after:
Inner Mongolia's largest airport, 14.3 km east of downtown Hohhot, handling just over 12.7 million passengers in 2025. Line 1 of the Hohhot Metro runs to the airport, which keeps the transfer into the city simple.

A new airport for the city, Hohhot Shengle International, is being prepared: in July 2026 the airport group was letting commercial space in its transport interchange. Check which airport a client's flight uses once Shengle opens.

Cargo passed 60,000 tonnes in 2025.
